title: 'Ship to Cuba' option shows up on Amazon.com amid diplomatic talks
summary: Amazon.com briefly displayed a "ship to Cuba" option on its website, leading to speculation that the company is preparing for shipments to the island amid warming diplomatic ties between the U.S. and Cuba. Although the option generated an error message when reporters attempted to use it, logistics experts suggest it indicates Amazon is testing the new service. Amazon has family ties to Cuba through CEO Jeff Bezos's adoptive father, Miguel Bezos, who was born there.

title: Amazon opens store on Alibaba's online marketplace Tmall
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has opened an online store on Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.'s Tmall.com as part of its strategy to expand in China. This move follows other Western retailers like Inditex, Burberry, and ASOS joining Tmall to boost their presence in the Chinese market. Amazon's store on Tmall sells imported food, shoes, toys, and kitchenware, while it also operates its own e-commerce site in China.

title: Mall Owner Simon Property Bids for Rival Macerich to Aim at High-End Shoppers (Published 2015)
summary: Simon Property Group, a major mall owner, has made an unsolicited bid to acquire rival Macerich Company for approximately $22.4 billion, including debt. This move by Simon aims to consolidate its position in the high-end mall market, which remains lucrative despite a general decline in traditional retail spaces. The bid highlights the increasing polarization in the retail landscape, where high-end malls continue to thrive by catering to wealthier shoppers.

title: Google hires new CFO: Morgan Stanley's Ruth Porat, 'the most powerful woman on Wall Street'
summary: Google has announced Ruth Porat, Morgan Stanley's CFO, will be joining the company as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective May 26. Porat, described as "the most powerful woman on Wall Street," will be returning to California, replacing the retiring Patrick Pichette. Google CEO Larry Page expressed enthusiasm for Porat's experience and contributions to the company's innovation and investments.

title: How This Family-Run Organic Grocer Is Taking on Whole Foods
summary: This article details the history and growth of Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, a family-run organic grocer founded by Margaret and Philip Isely in 1955. It highlights how the company, now with 93 stores and $521 million in sales, is challenging major competitors like Whole Foods and Sprouts by adhering to its founding principles of natural and organic products. The piece also discusses the management style of the second generation of Iselys and their ambitious expansion plans, including their decision to go public.

title: Android Installer Hijacking Vulnerability Could Expose Android Users to Malware
summary: Palo Alto Networks discovered a widespread "Android Installer Hijacking" vulnerability affecting nearly half of all Android users in March 2015. This vulnerability allows attackers to replace legitimate Android apps downloaded from third-party stores with malware without user knowledge, gaining full access to the compromised device. Palo Alto Networks worked with Google, Samsung, and Amazon to address the flaw and released a scanner app to help users identify if their devices are vulnerable.

title: The 'most powerful woman on Wall Street' just became Google's new CFO
summary: Ruth Porat, formerly the CFO of Morgan Stanley and once dubbed "the most powerful woman on Wall Street," has been appointed as Google's new CFO, replacing Patrick Pichette. She is set to begin her role on May 26 and will report directly to CEO Larry Page. Porat joins Google at a critical time when the company is facing investor concerns over slowing search advertising revenue growth.

title: Google Hires Morgan Stanley's Ruth Porat As Chief Financial Officer
summary: Google has hired Ruth Porat, Morgan Stanley's chief financial officer, to become its new CFO. Porat, who has extensive experience in banking for tech companies and senior M&A roles, will start in May. This move follows the departure of Google's previous CFO, Patrick Pichette, and highlights a trend of Wall Street executives moving to Silicon Valley.

title: Morgan Stanley CFO Ruth Porat to be Google’s new CFO
summary: Ruth Porat, Morgan Stanley's Chief Financial Officer, is moving to Google Inc. to take on the same role, a highly significant shift from Wall Street to Silicon Valley. This move underscores the changing economic power dynamics between the two sectors and Google's increasing prominence, especially as the finance industry continues to face post-financial-crisis scrutiny. Porat's appointment is also notable given Silicon Valley's ongoing challenges in hiring and promoting women in tech.

title: Measuring product-development vitality
summary: The article discusses the "Vitality Index," a key corporate R&D performance metric that measures the percentage of total company sales from new products. It explores the challenges in defining "new product" and its lifespan, highlighting the varied approaches companies take. The author also provides benchmarks for different levels of vitality and the impact of the chosen "N" value (length of time a product is considered new) on reported figures and corporate strategy.

title: Sunny Days: Hyatt Credits OpenText Cloud for 'World Class' Intranet
summary: Hyatt Hotels has dramatically improved its intranet, "Hyatt Connect," leading to a 500 percent increase in use among its 75,000 employees over five years. The Chicago-based hotel chain credits OpenText's cloud infrastructure for providing a cost-effective, scalable, and supportive solution that offers 24/7 support and helps manage content and applications. This move shifted Hyatt from a basic internal portal to a "world-class" intranet that facilitates communication and operations for its global workforce.

title: The Absolute Strangest Thing You Can Now Buy on Amazon
summary: Amazon's new Home Services marketplace offers a variety of professional services, including the unusual option to hire goat grazers. Customers can hire goats to manage vegetation, with the added bonus of natural fertilizer. This isn't Amazon's first interaction with goats, as Amazon Japan previously used them on its grounds.

title: Amazon's Dash button--Not an April Fools' joke
summary: Amazon launched its new "Dash" button, a small electronic device allowing users to instantly reorder frequently used household items like coffee, detergent, or toilet paper with a single press. The device connects to a user's Amazon account via Wi-Fi and sends an order, which can be canceled within 30 minutes, ensuring only one order is placed regardless of multiple clicks. This product is initially available by invitation only to Amazon Prime members.

title: March of the robots is key to new stock index created by Dallas firm
summary: Dallas-based Robo-Stox LLC has created the first global stock index dedicated to tracking the robotics and automation industry's market performance, similar to the S&P 500 for US stocks. The Robo-Stox Global Robotics and Automation Index comprises 82 stocks from 15 countries and the US, including companies like Siemens Co., Rockwell Automation Inc., and iRobot Corp. CEO Travis Briggs believes the robotics and automation sector is poised for significant growth, mirroring the early days of the internet, but with "real companies doing real things" and generating revenue.
